title: active-gel comets: a stronger regulator gives longer, sperm-like comets (up to 26 body lengths) but still only 1-3 persistent splits per run against 74-134 merges; where substrate is low enough to stop nucleation, nothing forms at all
summary: Extension of 20261025T1034-c09-active-gel-no-division. With substrate regrowth ks=0.05, raising the regulator's strength and rate (rho 1-1.5, kb 0.03-0.07) turns the comets into heads with long regulator tails that swim 16-26 body lengths in t=300 (img/sheet_ks0.05_rho1.5_kb0.05_s0.png), and labkit counts 1-3 persistent splits per run (generation <= 2), but identities churn through 74-134 merges and new comets nucleate in the gaps; I see no clean comet fission in the sheets. Lowering the supply to ks=0.02-0.03 to suppress nucleation, with a strong regulator (rho 2-3, kb 0.1-0.2), gives no bodies at all on 16 runs: the regulator suppresses the contractile instability before any peak forms (img/sheet_ks0.03_rho2_kb0.1_s0.png). In this family, a regime with bodies but no spontaneous generation was not found.

finding.operator: self-laid regulator (strength rho, rate kb) of the contractile active-gel stress, with substrate regrowth ks
finding.control: scan rho 1-3, kb 0.03-0.2, ks 0.02-0.05 at zeta=60 on seeds 0 and 1 (28 labkit runs, T=300)
finding.result: ks=0.05: 1-3 persistent splits per run (gen <= 2), merges 74-134, max 16-26 body lengths; ks=0.02-0.03 with rho 2-3, kb 0.1-0.2: 0 bodies in 16/16 runs
